text:
sam: Heads-up: leadership approved a small SLA baseline change for enterprise customers. We need a short internal maintenance + validation dry-run to prove our burn-rate detection and soft-failover behavior before the customer roll. Window: Wed 01:30-02:30 UTC. Please review runbook and call out blockers. :loudspeaker:

elaine: What exactly changed in the SLA? will this affect alerting or billing?

sam: Change summary: for tier-enterprise customers we now guarantee 99.95% availability (previously 99.9%) but with a clarified burn-rate clause: if an incident causes >2x burn-rate for >15m we trigger a degraded-SLA flow (credits + mitigation). This is mostly policy; we need infra verification that our burn-rate detector and routing policy enforce the intended behavior. No immediate billing changes until legal finishes the rollout comms.

hiro: For the dry-run, what's in scope? any pools we must avoid touching?

sam: Scope: one prod region shard (shard-03) limited to 3% traffic shift to fallback pools, and non-prod Dedicated pools. Reserved Dedicated capacity is excluded. Steps: 1) enable dry-run flag that logs burn-rate events but doesn't auto-credit; 2) trigger a simulated traffic surge via injector; 3) verify fallback routing and soft-throttle; 4) confirm automated credit calcs are gated behind a manual approval flag.

elaine: Can you paste the command to enable dry-run? ops needs the exact flag.

sam: Sure:```
infractl feature-flag set sla.burnrate.dry_run true --scope=prod-shard-03
```
Also to revert:```
infractl feature-flag set sla.burnrate.dry_run false --scope=prod-shard-03
```

hiro: How do we simulate the surge? want to run a small canary first.

sam: Injector command we will use:
```
./traffic-injector --target=shard-03 --pattern=burst --qps=800 --duration=10m --auth=svc-sre
```
We'll run a 2m canary at 01:35 then the full 10m burst if metrics look good.

elaine: Alerting changes during the window? I'd rather avoid noisy pages.

sam: Plan: silence non-critical latency channels; keep burn-rate pages active but route them to an SRE-only escalation for the dry-run. Set temporary page threshold for p99 to 7s for 20m to avoid expected noise. We will not auto-apply credits during dry-run.

hiro: What metrics to collect and where should I drop the post-run TL;DR?

sam: Collect p95/p99, error-rate, burn-rate multiplier, routing decision logs, and credit-calc debug logs. Post the TL;DR in this thread and upload the CSV to the runbook page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/sla/dryrun-2087. TL;DR template in runbook.

ops-bot: Scheduled reminder: SLA dry-run starts in 24h. Affected services: routing-layer, billing-calc, edge-router.

elaine: One blocker: infra has maintenance on the billing DB the same night. Could cause partial visibility for credit-calc logs. Ops, can you coordinate to move or we abort?

hiro: I'll ping infra now. If the billing DB is offline we'll skip the credit-calc verification step and mark it as manual check later.

sam: Good. Action items: hiro confirm billing DB status, ops apply silences 10m before start, run one 2m canary at 01:35 then proceed if OK. Please ACK if you reviewed runbook and have no blockers.

elaine: ack :thumbsup:

hiro: ack, pinged infra (waiting).

sre-bot: Thread pinned to channel by sam.
